text:
maria: kicking off a quick note — ran the internal load sweep (burst window experiments) against staging earlier and we saw intermittent 5xx (~2-3%) during the 10–25s mark of the burst. profile used: profiles/burst-1m. Not hitting obvious quota numbers on the dashboard, but requests are getting 503 with 'service_unavailable' from gateway. anyone available to triage?

simon: on it. can you paste the exact k6/wrk command + the response sample? also which model/route?

maria: sure — command was:
```bash
./scripts/run-loadtest.sh --profile burst-1m --target staging --concurrency 120 --rps 600
```
route: /v1/generate (model: redwood-13b-quant)
sample response headers/body:
```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: f2a8c1a2
{
  "error": {"type": "service_unavailable", "message": "node overloaded, please retry"}
}
```

maria: dashboard snapshot showed token_bucket tokens remaining ~ 60% at time, and pool utilization about 70%.

jen: two quick suspects: 1) short-term burst window on rate limiter (burst credits deplete then refill slower than we think), 2) queueing in front of runtime (max inflight reached causing 503 fallback). did you capture the per-route rate-limiter logs?

maria: yes, attached excerpt from rate-limiter logs (trimmed):
```
[1972000008] route=/v1/generate client=org-123 bucket_tokens=300 bucket_capacity=500 drained=300 refill_rate_per_sec=5
[1972000014] route=/v1/generate client=org-123 bucket_tokens=0 drained=500 refill_rate_per_sec=5 -> throttle_apply=500
[1972000020] route=/v1/generate client=org-123 queue_length=85 inflight=240 inflight_limit=250 -> fallback=503
```

dara: interesting — the logs show a bucket drain to zero quite fast (drained=500). But tokens=300 earlier is odd — are we mixing per-minute (TPM) vs per-second refills in the metric view? dashboard may be aggregating across windows.

qa-bot: checksum of loadtest profile: burst-1m -> steady_rps=200, burst_rps=600 for 60s, users=120. duration=10m.

simon: can we repro with a single client id so we can isolate per-customer bucket behavior (avoid multiple orgs consuming shared pool)? also try lowering concurrency to rule out inflight limits.

maria: repro attempt 2 with single API key and lower concurrency:
```bash
./scripts/run-loadtest.sh --profile burst-1m --target staging --apikey key-test-01 --concurrency 40 --rps 600
```
result: still seeing spikes of 503 at ~12s, but queue_length peaked lower (~40) and inflight peaked ~180. rate-limiter log snippet:
```
[1972000120] route=/v1/generate client=org-123 bucket_tokens=200 bucket_capacity=500
[1972000126] route=/v1/generate client=org-123 bucket_tokens=0 drained=500 refill_rate_per_sec=5 throttle_apply=500
[1972000132] route=/v1/generate client=org-123 inflight=180 inflight_limit=200 -> fallback=503
```

jen: refill_rate_per_sec=5 seems low relative to burst. If refill is set to support TPM but burst is expressed in RPS, mismatch occurs: bucket empties then takes ~100s to refill fully. we should verify how we compute refill_rate from RPM/TPM config.

dara: noted. config excerpt from rate limiter service (staging):
```yaml
rate_limits:
  - route: /v1/generate
    tpm: 12000
    rpm: 2000
    burst_capacity: 500
    refill_policy: token_per_second: tpm / 60
    inflight_limit: 250
```

simon: there it is — token_per_second uses tpm/60 which is correct for steady state, but our burst profile temporarily exceeds rpm/rps by 3x. burst_capacity=500 is not enough to sustain 600 RPS for 60s — 500 tokens covers ~500 requests only. after that we fall back. we likely need either bigger burst capacity, higher refill (token-per-second during burst), or smoothing at the loadtest generator (throttle up slower).

maria: fair. but previous docs suggested burst_capacity should be about 2x peak_rps * burst_seconds to avoid transient 503 on short bursts. we used 500 (just guessed). maybe bump to 1200.

jen: quick math: target burst 600rps for 60s => 36k tokens. But if steady refill gives 200rps equivalent (tpm/60), net deficit huge. tokens aren't meant to fully cover long sustained bursts — that's what reserved capacity/dedicated is for. For hosted defaults we should pick safe defaults that avoid 503 for typical developer bursts (short 10–30s), not 60s sustained at 3x baseline. Suggest policy: default burst window considered 30s and cap burst capacity = baseline_rps * 2 * 30.

dara: agree. propose action items:
- run param sweep to find minimal burst_capacity to keep <0.5% 503 for burst durations {10s,30s,60s} at burst multipliers {2x,3x}. (simon + qa)
- verify refill_rate computation and add explicit comment in config about token_per_second = tpm / 60 vs tpm / (60 * smoothing) (jen)
- add test harness in CI that simulates single-key bursts and asserts <1% error for default profile (maria + qa)

simon: I'll start sweep jobs — planning matrix: baseline_rps values {100,200,400}, burst_multipliers {2,3}, burst_secs {10,30,60}, burst_capacity candidates {baseline*0.5*secs, baseline*1*secs, baseline*2*secs, baseline*3*secs}. will run on staging with a single API key and collect rate-limiter traces + runtime inflight metrics.

maria: thanks. one more wrinkle: we saw some correlation with specific model (13b-quant) where generation latency spikes ~2-3x under load; that increases inflight times and makes inflight_limit the bottleneck earlier. we should add model-latency factor into the sweep or cap concurrency to avoid conflating rate limiter vs runtime capacity. put as a checkbox for the sweep.

jen: good catch. add model_latency_factor test: run both small (2B) and large (13B) models and annotate inflight time percentiles.

qa-bot: scheduling sweep jobs now. ETA ~ 45m for initial results. logs will be posted back to this thread.

deploy-bot: new artifact created: load-sweep-results/1972000000/run-1 -> https://ci.internal/load-sweep/1972000000

maria: thanks — will wait for results. for the default config doc change: i'm drafting a small blurb in docs explaining burst semantics and recommended defaults for hosted vs dedicated. will post PR after we have sweep numbers.

simon: initial sweep summary (posted 30m later):
- 10s bursts at 2x: burst_capacity = baseline*1*10 gave 0.01% 503, fine.
- 30s bursts at 2x: burst_capacity = baseline*2*30 required to get <0.5% 503 for 13B; baseline*1*30 failed.
- 60s bursts at 3x: even baseline*3*60 still had 0.8% 503 due to runtime latencies increasing inflight. conclusion: our default burst_capacity should be tuned for 30s windows; longer sustained bursts need Dedicated/Reserved.

maria: great data — i'll update the docs: recommended hosted defaults -> burst_window=30s, burst_capacity ~= baseline_rps * 2 * 30, inflight_limit = baseline_concurrency * 2 (guarded by model profile).

jen: and I'll add a follow-up to config: explicit metric names and how refill is computed. also propose adding a telemetry alert if observed 503s > 0.5% during a configured short burst window.

dara: next steps captured. thanks team. :thumbsup:

maria: will file a support KB for customers explaining why 60s+ sustained bursts may see 503 and recommending dedicated capacity for that pattern.

simon: results artifacts: https://ci.internal/load-sweep/1972000000/summary.json (metrics + traces)

maria: closing the loop once PRs land. if anyone sees similar in prod, ping me @maria immediately and include the request-id samples.

jen: ack — thanks everyone.
